owner: Patrick Craven, Top Shelf Service LLC

ARCH-D01.decision: Approve a modular monolith with one initial backend deployment and explicit logical module boundaries.

support_planes.constraint: May observe/report but must not alter authorization or command outcomes.
Not an application runtime authority until an approved runtime requirement requires it.
Owns governance semantics but is not a production business module.

ARCH-D01.rationale: TransactionControl owns runtime reconciliation state and a registered command, so it requires an owning runtime component. Governance and VerificationEvidence do not currently justify production business modules; Observability is a runtime support concern constrained by C53.

ARCH-D02.decision: Approve logical layering and enforce code dependencies separately from governance precedence.
code_dependency_rules: Domain must not import Application, Infrastructure, HTTP/UI frameworks, or transport adapters.
Application may depend on Domain and defines orchestration/use-case boundaries.
Infrastructure implements persistence/provider ports required by Domain/Application and may depend inward on their contracts.
Interfaces may depend on Application and transport schemas but must not contain domain rules or direct persistence access.
Generated artifacts may depend on K00 but must not invent semantics.

ARCH-D03.decision: Approve explicit cross-domain command/query boundaries with single-writer enforcement.
write_rules: Only the owning module may mutate its authoritative state.
Cross-domain writes invoke the owning module through a registered command/application interface.
No module may import another module's repository or issue SQL against another module's owned persistence.

Application orchestration may coordinate multiple owning command handlers inside one transaction context when an active contract requires atomicity; shared transaction context does not transfer write authority.
read_rules: Cross-domain reads use explicit read/query interfaces or approved snapshots supplied by the owning module.
Authorization may consume authoritative Identity/Organization facts read-only and may not mutate them.
Client-supplied scope or IDs never become authority merely by crossing an interface.

ARCH-D04.decision: Defer exact package/app directory names to implementation planning after logical architecture approval.
constraints: No physical layout may collapse domain ownership boundaries.
No package placement may allow Interfaces to bypass Application or Domain.
Persistence model and transport route inventory remain later build stages.

ARCH-D05.decision: Do not introduce microservices, a message broker, or an event-bus dependency as part of the initial architecture baseline.
constraints: Approved domain events may exist as semantic facts, but architecture must not synthesize or depend on candidate events.
In-process command/query boundaries are the default integration mechanism for the modular monolith.
Service extraction requires later evidence and an approved architecture revision.

architecture_rules.rule: Teach is a modular monolith by default; initial backend business modules share one deployment boundary.
Every mutable fact has one owning runtime component and one write path.
Cross-domain mutation occurs only through the owning module's registered command/application boundary.
Cross-domain repository imports and foreign-table writes are forbidden.
Domain code is transport-agnostic and infrastructure-agnostic.
Application orchestrates use cases; Interfaces adapt HTTP/UI/jobs/CLI/agents into Application.
Infrastructure implements persistence/provider ports; it does not own business semantics.
Authorization, transaction, audit, and reconciliation rules remain deterministic and agent-independent.
Observability is side-effect-neutral with respect to authorization and request outcomes.
Candidate K00 semantics are not architecture authority and cannot be consumed by implementation.
Persistence schema design is deferred until the Persistence Model stage; architecture defines ownership/boundaries, not tables.
Transport route/schema design is deferred until the Transport Interfaces stage; /api/v1 and C41 constraints remain controlling.
Microservices and broker infrastructure are deferred until evidence justifies extraction and an approved revision authorizes it.

acceptance_targets: Architecture test: Domain packages import no HTTP/UI framework and no Infrastructure package.
Architecture test: Interfaces import no database client/repository implementation.
Architecture test: cross-domain mutation call sites target registered application commands, not foreign repositories.
Architecture test: every persisted mutable aggregate maps to exactly one owning module before persistence implementation is accepted.
Architecture test: RuntimeAgent/AutomationActor paths cross the same Application/Domain boundary as human transports.
Architecture test: no candidate event, command proposal, relationship, invariant, or decision table is referenced as implementation authority.
explicitly_not_decided: Exact package names and directory layout.
ORM table design, keys, indexes, and migrations.
HTTP route inventory beyond already-active C41 constraints.
Any of the 9 remaining missing semantic candidates.
Any of the 8 discovery-blocked command proposals.
